text:
sara: FYI found a weird case during backup audit: snapshot s-2026-03-22-42 shows `encryption: CMK` in the manifest but object metadata `x-amz-server-side-encryption: AES256`. restore-service returned success but there's no KMS Decrypt/GenerateDataKey in CloudTrail for that snapshot id.

mike: that mismatch smells like header transformation in the upload path. can we get the uploader logs + multipart assembly trace? which uploader SA did the upload?

backup-bot: snapshot-uploader v2.4.0 started multipart upload s-2026-03-22-42 uploader_sa=svc-backup-staging parts=8

leo: I merged a multipart optimization yesterday that normalizes chunk metadata to reduce header size. PR 6901. It runs in the gateway and in the assembler. I did NOT expect it to remove sse headers but it's plausible if header canonicalization mis-detected the key.

anita: important: if SSE-C or AES headers replaced CMK metadata, KMS wouldn't be called and CloudTrail won't show grants. treat snapshot as potentially unencrypted-at-rest until verified. quarantine in catalog and block restores.

sara: agreed. I'll lock the snapshot in the catalog now and add an incident tag. also emailing compliance: "Potential unencrypted backup observed".

mike: I'll run CloudTrail query: `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=s-2026-03-22-42 --start-time '2026-03-22T16:30:00Z' --end-time '2026-03-22T17:30:00Z'` and `aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/backup-staging`.

leo: rolling back the assembler change to be safe. `git checkout -b rollback/6901 && ./deploy gateway --tag rollback-6901` will begin in 10m. I can also reprocess the snapshot parts after rollback.

anita: add a short detection to SIEM: correlate restore-service "restore:success" entries with CloudTrail KMS events for the same snapshot id within +-60s. If none found, create high-priority alert (PD). Keep it experimental and mute for known maintenance windows.

ops-oncall: can we also check RBAC for svc-backup-staging? there was a brief role rotation window at 16:55 where the SA replacement ran. kube-audit shows a role-bind update. if the SA lost kms:Encrypt permission temporarily, that could explain it.

sara: good catch. I'm pulling role-change audit now.

mike: also check uploader binary version across pods; if older pods didn't get the header-fix, parts could be mixed. run: `kubectl get pods -l app=snapshot-uploader -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}:{.spec.containers[0].image}\n'` to validate.

leo: noted. I'll coordinate pod restarts post-rollback. reprocess script: `./tools/reprocess s-2026-03-22-42 --force` but only after we confirm manifest/metadata alignment.

anita: put a temporary guard in restore-service: no auto-restore for snapshots where object metadata and manifest disagree on encryption. Return 409 and note reason in response. That prevents silent restores until we confirm.

sara: assigning: leo = rollback + reprocess, mike = cloudtrail + kms grant checks, anita = detection rule + restore guard, ops-oncall = RBAC role-change correlation + notify infra. I'll update the incident channel and compliance thread.

mike: quick update: CloudTrail shows GenerateDataKey events for key alias/backup-staging at 16:31:05 but not tied to the snapshot object id. list-grants returns a grant created at 16:30:58 by svc-backup-prod, not staging. odd cross-service. digging.

ops-oncall: kube-audit shows `rolebinding/backup-svc-rotate` applied 16:55:12 and kubeproxy restarted a node at 16:56. possible transient auth gap. collecting more logs.

leo: rollback pushed, monitoring deploy. I'll open a PR to add a unit test that ensures multipart assembler preserves all x-amz-* encryption headers.

anita: once we confirm root cause, create an internal postmortem with timeline, blast radius, and remediation (device-level validation, SIEM rule, RBAC hardening, restore guard). recommend a one-week hold on cross-region reuploads until we add an automated header/verifier step.

sara: thanks everyone. tagging compliance and legal for visibility. will write a short exec summary when we know scope. :white_check_mark:
